result.title: Event-WAM: Learning to Act with Event-Derived Futures
result.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) leverage future visual modeling for robotic action learning, with recent studies exploring alternative or complementary objectives beyond conventional RGB prediction. We introduce Event-WAM, which incorporates event-derived visual changes as auxiliary future supervision alongside RGB. Event-WAM constructs temporally structured event representations from RGB demonstrations and encodes them using a frozen pretrained RGB video VAE, without training an event-specific VAE. Joint RGB--Event latent flow matching provides appearance- and change-oriented supervision without requiring event observations or explicit future generation at inference. Across simulated benchmarks, Event-WAM maintains comparable performance under standard conditions, while robustness gains under perturbations are benchmark-dependent, including improvements on LIBERO-Plus. Real-world evaluations further demonstrate improved manipulation success under both standard and unseen perturbation conditions. Further analyses show that policy improvements are not consistently accompanied by higher future prediction fidelity, suggesting the potential of change-oriented supervision for action learning.

AI.brief_summary: Event-WAM 把事件导出的视觉变化作为辅助未来监督，与 RGB 一起在冻结视频 VAE 的 latent 空间做联合 flow matching 来训练机器人操作策略，推理时无需事件输入或显式预测未来。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 latent 未来变化作辅助监督、且发现预测保真度提升与策略收益并不同步，可供核查 LVR 中视觉监督信号与该监督对最终输出的贡献分配问题；但属机器人世界模型，与 VLM 推理期 latent 状态生成无直接联系。
